## Synthesis Overview

This PR bootstraps the Opencode migration by adding `opencode.json`, placeholder `.opencode/` directories, ADR 009, a PRD, a task breakdown, and a research report. The three reviewers agreed on one unanimous finding (commit message quality) and two reviewers flagged the relative `.chromadb` path risk. The main substantive divergence was between GPT — which argued the PR is not ready for merge because several existing planning docs now contain false historical claims — and Claude and Gemini, which treated the PR as approvable with follow-up warnings. One Gemini finding (`"plugin"` field name) was assessed as a false positive based on verified project documentation. Claude produced by far the most detailed review, surfacing four additional singular findings that warrant follow-up.

**Model Agreement Score: 6/10** — The three models agreed on the commit message issue, but diverged on merge readiness, scope of documentation concerns, and unique findings. Gemini's review was the most narrow, raising only two findings, while Claude's was the most comprehensive with six.

[U-W-01] Commit 221fe7e uses bare "updates" message — violates project convention
Severity: Warning
Category: Style
File: git history — commit 221fe7e
Lines: general
Detail: All three models independently identified that the second commit on this branch
  uses the message "updates", which does not meet the project's commit convention requiring
  a semantic prefix (feat:, fix:, docs:, chore:), an imperative mood description, and
  an issue reference. The changed files in that commit are documentation and planning
  artefacts (docs/planning/, .github/research/, .github/notes/), so the correct form
  would be something like:
    docs(opencode): add ADR 009, PRD, task breakdown, and research report (#224)
  This is an existing commit — squash or amend is not required if the project does not
  enforce a clean log on development, but the pattern should not recur.
Models: Claude ✓  GPT ✓  Gemini ✓
Suggestion: Rewrite the commit to a descriptive conventional form. Consider adding a
  commit-msg hook (commitlint) to prevent recurrence.

### ★★☆ Majority Findings (Two of Three Models Agree)

```
[M-W-01] Relative --data-dir .chromadb path has no CWD anchor in Opencode MCP config
Severity: Warning
Category: Correctness
File: opencode.json
Lines: 8
Detail: The Opencode MCP spec has no equivalent to VS Code's "cwd" field (confirmed in
  the project's own research report, [U-03] footnote). Without a working-directory anchor,
  `uvx chroma-mcp --data-dir .chromadb` resolves the path relative to whatever directory
  Opencode uses when spawning the MCP process. If Opencode always spawns from the project
  root (where opencode.json lives), the path resolves correctly. If it does not — or if a
  developer invokes opencode from a subdirectory — the process silently creates a new,
  empty .chromadb/ in the wrong location rather than failing with an error. This silent
  misdirection is the primary risk.
  Claude raised this as a Warning; GPT raised it as a Suggestion. The Warning classification
  is retained here because the failure mode (silent wrong-path creation) is worse than a
  simple error, and empirical verification of Opencode's spawn CWD is not yet recorded.
Models: Claude ✓  GPT ✓  Gemini ✗
Dissenting view: Gemini did not raise this finding at all, treating the MCP config as
  correct as-is.
Suggestion: (a) Document the constraint visibly: "opencode must be launched from the
  project root; the chroma MCP uses a relative --data-dir path." Place this in
  docs/features/opencode-runtime.md (Task 10) or as an inline comment.
  (b) During Task 2 or Task 9, verify empirically that Opencode anchors MCP spawn CWD
  to the project root. If it does not, switch to an absolute path via env-var interpolation:
  "--data-dir", "{env:PROJECT_ROOT}/.chromadb".
```

```
[S-W-01] Existing planning docs now contain false completion claims about Opencode removal
Severity: Warning
Category: Documentation
File: docs/planning/python-native-migration/prd.md (lines 148, 163);
      docs/planning/python-native-migration/tasks.md (line 298);
      docs/planning/opencode-migration/SUPERSEDED.md (line 31);
      docs/features/python-native-foundation.md (line 115)
Lines: see above
Detail: The python-native-migration PRD contains completed [x] acceptance criteria
  asserting that (line 148) "All files under .opencode/, all .ts files, opencode.json …
  are removed from the repository" and (line 163) "AGENTS.md, README.md, and docs/
  contain no references to OpenCode, opencode.json, .opencode/, or the TypeScript tool
  layer." Both claims are now false: this PR reintroduces opencode.json, .opencode/
  directories, and references to Opencode throughout the new docs/ planning tree.
  Synthesizer verification confirmed lines 148 and 163 exist verbatim with [x] markers.
  The files cited by GPT were verified to contain the claimed stale text.
Model: GPT
Assessment: Genuine finding, verified. However, context matters: these documents describe
  a migration that already occurred (python-native migration), and the completion marks
  are historically accurate. The current PR is a *new* migration in the opposite direction
  with its own ADR and PRD. A reader of only the python-native docs would have an
  incorrect picture of the repository. The question is whether cleanup belongs in this PR
  or in a dedicated follow-up task. GPT argues it belongs in this PR; Claude and Gemini
  did not raise it. Given that this is a bootstrap PR with bounded scope, a follow-up task
  is a reasonable alternative, but the stale claims should not remain indefinitely.
Suggestion: Either update the stale docs in this PR (add an "SUPERSEDED by ADR 009" note
  to the affected files) or create a dedicated cleanup task in tasks.md. The
  docs/planning/python-native-migration/prd.md lines 148 and 163 are the highest
  priority because they are active completion criteria that are now incorrect.
```

```
[S-W-03] tasks.md sequencing rule #3 mislabels Task 4 and misstates batch count
Severity: Warning
Category: Documentation
File: docs/planning/copilot-to-opencode-migration/tasks.md
Lines: sequencing rule #3 (approx. lines 13–16)
Detail: Rule #3 reads: "The agent migration is split into four batches (Tasks 5, 6, 7, 8)
  by family…" Two errors: (a) Task 4 (Orchestrator V3 migration) is missing from the
  parenthetical — there are five agent migration tasks (4–8), not four. Omitting Task 4
  makes it appear independent with no sequencing constraint. (b) "The Orchestrator family
  (Task 5)" mislabels Task 5, which is actually the specialist sub-agents (Coder, Test
  Writer, Documenter, Browser, Reflection). Task 4 is the Orchestrator V3 itself. The
  causal reasoning is also inverted: the rule says Task 5 "goes first" because sub-agents
  need a working orchestrator, but Task 5 IS the sub-agent migration — it should follow
  Task 4, not precede it.
Model: Claude
Assessment: Genuine documentation error. A future implementer reading this rule in
  isolation could run Task 5 before Task 4, which would break the dispatch validation
  the sequencing rule is designed to enforce.
Suggestion: Replace rule #3 with:
  "3. The agent migration is split into five tasks (4–8). Task 4 (Orchestrator V3)
     must land first because Tasks 5–8 all depend on a working orchestrator to validate
     dispatch. Tasks 5–8 are batched by family (specialist sub-agents, reviewer,
     researcher, auditor+standalone) so each PR is independently reviewable."
```

```
[S-I-02] opencode-rules@latest is not pinned to a specific version
Severity: Suggestion
Category: Style
File: opencode.json
Lines: 4
Detail: The plugin declaration uses @latest rather than a pinned semver. If
  opencode-rules releases a breaking change to its frontmatter schema or glob
  evaluation, rule files under .opencode/rules/ could silently stop matching. This
  is low risk in the bootstrap PR (no rule files exist yet), but will matter once
  Task 3 creates .opencode/rules/chromadb.md.
Model: Claude
Assessment: Valid long-term hygiene concern. No immediate risk at this stage.
Suggestion: Pin to a specific version once Task 3 validates plugin behaviour. Use
  @latest only during initial evaluation; pin before the full agent migration (Tasks 4–8).
```

## Divergence Analysis

```
[D-01] Topic: Merge readiness
Claude says: Approved with warnings — none of the findings block merge on their own,
  though F-02 and F-03 will cause downstream confusion if left open.
GPT says: Not ready for merge — the PR introduces an immediately contradictory repo
  state by restoring Opencode artefacts while several existing docs still assert they
  were fully removed. Wants documentation reconciled in the same PR.
Gemini says: Approved with minor fixes — after the commit message is cleaned up and
  the plugin field is verified, the branch is ready to merge.
Assessment: This is a 2-vs-1 split favouring merge with follow-up. GPT's concern is
  technically valid (verified stale docs exist) but arguably strict for a bounded
  bootstrap PR. The existing stale docs are in the python-native-migration history tree,
  which is a completed-and-superseded migration; adding an "SUPERSEDED by ADR 009"
  notation is appropriate but does not have to be a merge blocker. Claude's classification
  of F-02 and F-03 (ADR index gap, sequencing rule confusion) as pre-merge warnings is
  more calibrated to the scope. Recommended resolution: treat [S-W-01] as a
  pre-merge fix for the AGENTS.md/docs/ false claims (the most misleading ones), and
  schedule the historical archive files for a follow-up cleanup task.
Resolution: Majority position (merge with warnings) is correct, with [S-W-01] elevated
  to a required pre-merge fix for the AGENTS.md/docs/ boundary cases only.
```

```
[D-02] Topic: Severity of --data-dir CWD risk
Claude says: Warning — silent wrong-path creation is a correctness issue, not just a
  documentation concern.
GPT says: Suggestion — primarily a documentation gap; acceptable to document and
  verify in a follow-up task.
Gemini says: (not raised)
Assessment: Claude's Warning classification is better supported. The failure mode
  (silent creation of a new empty .chromadb/ in the wrong directory) is genuinely
  problematic: the developer would see a working MCP process with no data, with no
  error indicating what went wrong. This warrants more than a suggestion.
Resolution: Retained as Warning in [M-W-01].
```

```
[D-03] Topic: "plugin" vs "plugins" field name in opencode.json
Claude says: (not raised)
GPT says: (not raised)
Gemini says: Warning — the field should be "plugins" (plural); "plugin" may prevent
  the runtime from loading the plugin.
Assessment: FALSE POSITIVE. The project's own PRD (docs/planning/copilot-to-opencode-
  migration/prd.md, line 112 and line 150) explicitly specifies the field as
  `"plugin"` (singular) in both the spec and the acceptance criteria:
  "- [ ] opencode.json declares \"plugin\": [\"opencode-rules@latest\"]"
  This is a 2-vs-1 split against Gemini, confirmed by project documentation. The
  "plugin" field name is intentional and matches the project's own specification.
Resolution: Gemini's W-02 is excluded from consensus findings as a false positive.
```
